checks.check: Direct calls return frozen canonical absolute runtime paths only for the exact verified identity; tampered files/metadata, extra files, bad target/baseline, links and unsafe roots fail closed.
checks.evidence: runtime-store.ts verifies canonical identity, owned non-link ancestors, exact membership, file digests and modes before freezing the result and nested identity. Resolver tests exercise corruption, extras, identity mismatches, links and unsafe homes; daemon reports passing.

checks.check: A self-consistent rewritten receipt/inventory cannot replace the independently pinned expected inventory hash.
checks.evidence: Completion bytes are compared against policy-derived inventorySha256; verifyRuntimeInventory independently hashes inventory bytes against runtimeProfile. Tests forge both receipt and inventory, then inventory alone, and verify rejection and restoration.

checks.check: Resolver imports no application paths/DB/provider/source builder and performs no network, mkdir, controller lock, selection or application/Ollama traversal.
checks.evidence: Inspected resolver uses installer read primitives. The esbuild import-boundary test checks transitive inputs; runtime mocks restrict opens/readdir and reject mutations/downloads. No application, DB, provider or source-builder imports occur.

checks.check: Task-local fixtures prove this API; production consumer wiring is assessed in t8, not required prematurely for t2 validation.
checks.evidence: runtime-store.test.ts independently constructs protected official-profile copies and calls the resolver/content verifier directly. The task commit does not modify production consumers.

checks.check: Default canonical resolution accepts only exact published root/directories0500, metadata0400, files pinnedmode&~0222 with zero write bits and exact execute intent. Source-stage checks original modes; permission-transition accepts only root0700/0500 with every descendant protected. No arbitrary mixed subtree or old-home adoption, allocation or launch paths from a weak verifier flag.
checks.evidence: verifyRuntimeEntry implements those exact POSIX modes. resolveRuntimeStore always uses published verification; alternative lanes only classify rejection diagnostics. Tests exercise write/execute drift, mixed descendants, source-stage, transition and ignored weakening options.

checks.check: Use the exact LLD8 §4.3 runtime-invalid manual recovery, root-only unfinished and unsupported-development-layout messages. Manual text advises safely quoted root-only chmod, preservation/move and delete nothing, and explicitly disclaims product locking/all-consumer proof. Test spaces/Unicode/apostrophes and preservation; do not implement an operator move/recovery command.
checks.evidence: All three strings match LLD §4.3. The manual diagnostic test preserves corrupt bytes/root inode and uses a shell printf probe to verify single-argument quoting of a root containing spaces, Unicode and an apostrophe. No recovery command is implemented.

checks.check: For every rejection mutation, establish a positive baseline beforehand, assert its precise expected code/message and prove restoration succeeds; no bare rejects or shared broken fixture false positives. Protected-fixture mutation helpers may deliberately alter only their captured isolated homes.
checks.evidence: Most mutations use rejectedMutation with exact code/full-message assertions and successful resolution before/after. However, the bad-baseline 'other' case in runtime-store.test.ts only checks runtime-invalid and /ENOENT.*other/. It does not assert the precise expected diagnostic, so the required universal exact-diagnostic coverage and corresponding named rejection-matrix test are incomplete despite passing.

checks.check: Implement the proposed shared _owned-runtime-home.ts test helper using captured mkdtemp dev/inode/UID, retained child/resource closure and bounded nofollow checks. Restore directory ownerwrite only within that root after positive closure; never follow a link to chmod its target, mutate SDK/global/blocked roots or erase uncertain evidence. All adopting callers await cleanup, including allocation failure/after/finally. Prove cleanup/retention/refusal cases independently.
checks.evidence: Helper captures a newly allocated root identity, waits for retained children/resources, bounds traversal, rejects unknown links/replacements, and restores directory write through O_NOFOLLOW/O_DIRECTORY descriptors. Eight independent tests cover closure, links, replacement, uncertainty, allocation failure and bounds. Resolver allocation failure and finally paths await cleanup.

checks.check: Introduce the owned-home helper without turning raw/shared mutable SDK caches into cleanup targets. Resolver fixtures can seed the strict protected form independently before T4 is implemented; fixture APIs with asynchronous disposal are awaited by every changed caller.
checks.evidence: Only freshly allocated resolver homes are adopted. Official input caches and the writable source copy remain separate. Fixtures seed protected modes directly, and all changed resolver callers await asynchronous disposal.

verdict.reason: The task-scoped implementation and daemon checks pass, but the bad-baseline rejection lacks the precise expected-message assertion explicitly required for every rejection mutation.
